item.dc:creator: P. L. Krapivsky

item.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
item.description: arXiv:2611.14836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Stark, Georg K\"ostenberger, Nina D\"ornemann

item.title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
item.description: arXiv:2611.15549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.
item.dc:creator: Maike C. de Jongh, Antal A. J\'arai, Richard J. Boucherie, M. N. M. van Lieshout

item.title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.15803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{\Omega(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $\chi^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.
item.dc:creator: Debsurya De, Dmitriy Kunisky

item.title: Sharp Lower Bounds for Parallel Log-Concave Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.15849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many rounds of parallel queries are needed to sample from a smooth, strongly log-concave distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$? For every fixed condition number $\kappa \in (1, \infty)$, we prove that any sampler making polynomially many queries per round requires $\Omega_\kappa(\log d)$ rounds to achieve constant total variation error in the worst case. The lower bound holds even if queries return derivatives of all orders. Together with the first-order parallel Picard algorithm of \cite{zhou2025parallel}, this establishes a depth complexity of $\Theta_\kappa(\log d)$ for parallel log-concave sampling with $\operatorname{poly}(d)$ width. We then study centered Gaussian targets to understand how much width is needed at a given depth. From \cite{chewi2023query,zhou2026complexitygaussiansampling}, it is known that either one round of width $d$ or $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\kappa} \log d)$ rounds of constant width suffice for first-order Gaussian sampling. At fixed $\kappa$ we characterize the depth-width tradeoff interpolating between these regimes: when using $ \lceil c \log d\rceil$ rounds, if $0 < c < c_\star(\kappa)$ then the optimal width at constant TV error is $\widetilde{\Theta}(d^{1-c/c_\star(\kappa)})$, while if $c \geq c_\star(\kappa)$ then it is $\Theta_\kappa(1)$. Here, $c_\star(\kappa)$ is an explicit constant with $c_\star(\kappa) \sim \sqrt{\kappa} / 8$ as $\kappa \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Evan Dogariu

item.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.16007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(\sigma)$ to $L^q(\omega)$ for the operator $H_\sigma g(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,d\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $\omega$ is a $\sigma$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $\kappa_{p,q}$ in $C_*\le\kappa_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $\omega$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Os\k{e}kowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Kanjilal

item.title: Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sch\"utt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Sch\"utt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Th\"ale, Steffen Winter

item.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.16273v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.
item.dc:creator: Tin Tran, Liet Vo

item.title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.16457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(\alpha^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $\alpha\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.
item.dc:creator: Chuchu Chen, Xinyu Chen, Jialin Hong

item.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule
item.description: arXiv:2611.16541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)\Pi$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(\mu+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chang Yeh

item.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.16674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Lundblad, Stephan Wagner

item.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.16930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.
item.dc:creator: Jianbo Cui, Liying Sun

item.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.16978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Clemens Thalhammer

item.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.17002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.
item.dc:creator: Yingyu Zhao, Yunhao Zhao

item.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
item.description: arXiv:2611.17174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma is a system of point charges that repel each other logarithmically, in a uniform neutralizing background. When the inverse temperature $\beta$ is at most $2$, we prove that its correlations decay exponentially, and that its Gibbs state is unique among point processes whose fluctuations are controlled. This constitutes part of the fluid phase predicted by physicists. As a consequence, we obtain the existence of an infinite-volume limit, extending the Ginibre point process, which we call $\mathrm{Gin}_\beta$. We show that its truncated two-point function, at the scale of the Debye length, is given to first order in $\beta$ by the Debye-H\"uckel approximation.
item.dc:creator: Jeanne Boursier, Thomas Lebl\'e

item.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
item.description: arXiv:2611.17223v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{\delta_*}$, where ${\delta_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{\delta_*}^{-2}\log(n/{\delta_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Renato Paes Leme, Rad Niazadeh

item.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.17247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Shuoqing Deng, Daxin Huang, Dominykas Norgilas

item.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Kittle, Constantin Kogler

item.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2303.18112v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $\Phi^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Paolo Rinaldi

item.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: I. Order-Disorder Interface convergence
item.description: arXiv:2502.04129v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a $q$-state Potts model on the square grid when $q>4$ at the point $T_c(q)$ of its (discontinous) transition. This model exhibits exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures: $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). The current work deals with the Dobrushin order--disorder boundary conditions on a finite $N\times N$ box. Our main result is that this interface is a well-defined object, has $\sqrt{N}$ fluctuations, and converges to a Brownian bridge under diffusive scaling. The same holds also for the corresponding FK-percolation model for all $q>4$. Our proofs rely on a coupling between FK-percolation, the six-vertex model, and the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and on a detailed study of the latter. The coupling relates the interface in FK-percolation to a long subcritical cluster in the ATRC model. For this cluster we develop a ``renewal picture'' \`a la Ornstein-Zernike. This is based on fine mixing properties of the ATRC model that we establish using the link to the six-vertex model and its height function. Along the way, we derive various properties of the Ashkin-Teller model, such as Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics for its two-point function. In a companion work, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-order Dobrushin conditions. We show emergence of a free layer of width $\sqrt{N}$ between the two ordered phases (wetting) and establish convergence of its boundaries to two Brownian bridges conditioned not to intersect.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Dober, Alexander Glazman, S\'ebastien Ott

item.title: Optimal linear filtering of partially observed polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time
item.description: arXiv:2503.05588v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to filtering, smoothing, and prediction of polynomial processes that are partially observed. These problems are known to allow for an explicit solution in the simpler case of linear Gaussian state space models. The key insight underlying the present piece of research is that in linear filtering applications polynomial processes and their discrete-time counterpart are indistinguishable from Gaussian processes sharing their first two moments. We describe the construction of these Gaussian equivalents of polynomial processes and explicitly compute optimal linear filters, predictors and smoothers for polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time. The consideration of Gaussian equivalents also opens the door to parameter estimation and linear-quadratic optimal control in the context of polynomial processes.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kallsen, Ivo Richert

item.title: Homogenization theory of random walks in degenerate random environment
item.description: arXiv:2504.06690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent progress on the understanding of the Random Conductance Model is reviewed. A particular emphasis is on homogenization results such as functional central limit theorems, local limit theorems and heat kernel estimates for almost every realization of the environment, established for random walks among stationary ergodic conductances that are possibly unbounded but satisfy certain moment conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Andres

item.title: Exponentially Fading Memory Signature
item.description: arXiv:2507.03700v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the exponentially fading memory (EFM) signature, a time-invariant transformation of an infinite (possibly rough) path that serves as a mean-reverting analogue of the classical path signature. We construct the EFM-signature via rough path theory, carefully adapted to accommodate improper integration from minus infinity. The EFM-signature retains many of the key algebraic and analytical properties of classical signatures, including a suitably modified Chen identity, the linearization property, path-determinacy, and the universal approximation property. From the probabilistic perspective, the EFM-signature provides a "stationarized" representation, making it particularly well-suited for time-series analysis and signal processing overcoming the shortcomings of the standard signature. In particular, the EFM-signature of time-augmented Brownian motion evolves as a group-valued Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We establish its stationarity, Markov property, and exponential ergodicity in the Wasserstein distance, and we derive an explicit formula \`a la Fawcett for its expected value in terms of Magnus expansions. We also study linear combinations of EFM-signature elements and the computation of associated characteristic functions in terms of a mean-reverting infinite dimensional Riccati equation.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Abi Jaber, Dimitri Sotnikov

item.title: The limiting spectral distribution for sparse elliptic random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2508.04891v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies sparse elliptic random matrix models which generalize both the classical elliptic ensembles and sparse i.i.d. matrix models by incorporating correlated entries and a tunable sparsity parameter $p_n$. Each $n\times n$ matrix $X_n$ is formed by entry-wise multiplication of an elliptic random matrix by an elliptic matrix of Bernoulli($p_n$) variables, where $np_n$ tends to infinity at a sufficient rate, allowing for interpolation between dense and sparse regimes. The main result establishes that after appropriate normalization, the empirical spectral measures of these matrices converge weakly in probability to the uniform measure on a rotated ellipsoid in the complex plane as the dimension $n$ tends to infinity. Interestingly, the shape of the limiting ellipsoid depends not only on the mirrored entry-wise correlation structure, but also non-trivially on the sparsity limit $p=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}p_n$.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Carpenter, Sean O'Rourke

item.title: Parabolic equations with large long-range random potentials of arbitrary Hermite rank: convergence to Hermite-driven Feynman-Kac limits
item.description: arXiv:2512.08496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional heat equation with a large, rapidly oscillating random potential, obtained by applying a polynomial of arbitrary Hermite rank to a stationary Gaussian process with long-range dependence. When the correlations decay slowly enough, the solution does not homogenise to a deterministic limit. We prove that it converges in law, as a random field, to a Feynman-Kac functional driven by a Hermite process, which is fractional Brownian motion for Hermite rank one and the Rosenblatt process for Hermite rank two. The proof rests on an identity which expresses the exponent of the Feynman-Kac formula as a continuous functional of the integrated potential, so that neither local times of fractional processes nor exponential moments with respect to the potential are needed. We also show that the limit has moments of every order for Hermite rank one, and for Hermite rank two with a negative second Hermite coefficient, whereas for a positive coefficient its mean is infinite, although it is finite almost surely. A numerical experiment illustrates the convergence of the integrated potential to the Rosenblatt law.
item.dc:creator: Atef Lechiheb

item.title: Banach-Valued Carr\'e du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2512.08919v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carr\'e du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fr\'echet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carr\'e du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Solesne Bourguin, Simon Campese

item.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
item.description: arXiv:2512.24807v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus \Sigma$ is a $\kappa$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-\alpha}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $\alpha\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus \Sigma$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $\alpha$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Cho, Panki Kim, Renming Song, Zoran Vondra\v{c}ek

item.title: Universal concentration for sums under arbitrary dependence
item.description: arXiv:2601.03518v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a universal concentration bound for sums of random variables under arbitrary dependence, and we prove that it is asymptotically optimal for broad families of marginals admitting a uniform integrable tail-quantile envelope. The bound follows directly from the subadditivity of expected shortfall, a property well known in the risk-measure literature. Our sharpness result relies on an explicit construction of asymptotically extremal couplings. We furthermore provide practical sufficient conditions -- based on convex transformation order comparisons with exponential and power-law envelopes -- under which the bound admits simple, explicit tail profiles.
item.dc:creator: Cosme Louart, Sicheng Tan

item.title: Functional Stochastic Localization
item.description: arXiv:2602.03999v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Eldan's stochastic localization is a probabilistic construction that has proved instrumental to modern breakthroughs in high-dimensional geometry and the design of sampling algorithms. Motivated by sampling under non-Euclidean geometries and the mirror descent algorithm in optimization, we develop a functional generalization of Eldan's process that replaces Gaussian regularization with regularization by any positive integer multiple of a log-Laplace transform. We further give a mixing time bound on the Markov chain induced by our localization process, which holds if our target distribution satisfies a functional Poincar\'e inequality. Finally, we apply our framework to differentially private convex optimization in $\ell_p$ norms for $p \in [1, 2)$, where we improve state-of-the-art query complexities in a zeroth-order model.
item.dc:creator: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian

item.title: Limiting Behavior of Randomly Perturbed Diffusions with Invariant Repelling Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.07157v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study small perturbations of diffusion processes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that leave invariant a finite collection of hypersurfaces. Each surface is assumed to be repelling for the unperturbed process, and the unperturbed motion on each of the surfaces is assumed to be ergodic. These surfaces separate the space into a finite number of domains, each of which carries an invariant measure of the unperturbed process. We describe the asymptotics of the densities of the invariant measures near the invariant surfaces. We then describe the asymptotic behavior of the perturbed process: at different time scales (depending on the size of the perturbation), metastable distributions are described in terms of linear combinations of the ergodic invariant measures of the unperturbed system. The coefficients in the linear combination depend on the time scale but are shown not to depend on the perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Koralov, Chenglin Liu

item.title: Averaging Dynamics and Wong-Zakai approximations for a Fast-Slow Navier-Stokes System Driven by fractional Brownian Motion
item.description: arXiv:2602.08680v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Fast-Slow system of coupled two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in which the fast component is perturbed by an additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $\H>\frac{1}{3}$. Using rough path theory, we establish subsequential convergence in law of the slow component, with limiting dynamics depending on the Hurst parameter and the noise scaling. For $\H<\frac12$, an averaging regime yields a deterministic Navier-Stokes equation with an additional It\^o-Stokes drift. Under a stronger noise scaling, corresponding to a Wong-Zakai approximation, and a centering condition on the quadratic fast dynamics, we obtain a Navier-Stokes equation driven by fractional transport noise. For $\H>\frac12$, the transport-noise limit holds in the Wong-Zakai regime without this centering condition, with integration understood in the Young sense.
item.dc:creator: Eliseo Luongo, Francesco Triggiano

item.title: On the Uniqueness of Fr\'echet Means for Polytope Norms
item.description: arXiv:2603.15785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fr\'echet means are a popular type of average for non-Euclidean datasets, defined as those points that minimise the average squared distance to a set of data points. We consider the behaviour of sample Fr\'echet means on normed spaces whose unit ball is a polytope; this setting is particularly important for semi-discrete data, but is rarely covered by existing literature on Fr\'echet means, which focuses primarily on manifolds and spaces with bounded Alexandrov curvature. We study the geometry of the set of Fr\'echet means over polytope normed spaces, with a focus on dimension and probabilistic conditions for uniqueness. In particular, we provide a geometric characterisation of the threshold sample size at which Fr\'echet means have a positive probability of being unique, and we prove that this threshold is at most one more than the dimension of our space. This geometric characterisation presents a novel framework for computing the unique Fr\'echet mean sample threshold, which we demonstrate in the case of the $\ell_1$, $\ell_{\infty}$ and tropical norms. In particular, we show that the $\ell_1$ sample threshold is always 3, but the $\ell_{\infty}$ and tropical sample thresholds grow at different rates with the dimension of our space.
item.dc:creator: Roan Talbut, Andrew McCormack, Anthea Monod

item.title: Hydrodynamic Limit of the Directed Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2604.08154v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the Euler (hyperbolic) hydrodynamic limit for the directed exclusion process (DEP), a one-dimensional conservative interacting particle system that preserves particle--hole symmetry while breaking left--right symmetry. The proof relies on an explicit multi-process coupling, which guarantees a strong form of attractiveness and macroscopic stability for the particle system. Further open questions about DEP are briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Saada (MAP5 - UMR 8145,UPCit{\'e}), Federico Sau (UNIMI), Assaf Shapira (UPCit{\'e},MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: On ergodicity of the SAGA-LD algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2604.12815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The so-called SAGA-LD algorithm is used for efficient sampling from high-dimensional distributions in machine learning. Its intricate dynamics resists standard approaches of Markov chain theory. We prove, using a model-specific method, that SAGA-LD converges to a limiting distribution and a law of large numbers holds.
item.dc:creator: Mikl\'os R\'asonyi

item.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: II. Wetting and Brownian watermelon
item.description: arXiv:2604.21669v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $q$-state Potts model is an archetypical model for various types of phase transitions. We consider it on the square grid and focus on the regime where it undergoes a discontinuous transition, that is $q>4$. At the transition point $T_c(q)$, there are exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures (pure phases): $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). This work establishes for the first time the wetting phenomenon in a precise geometric form and in the entire regime of discontinuity $q>4$: at $T_c(q)$, between two ordered phases a disordered layer emerges and, in the diffusive scaling, its boundaries converge to a pair of Brownian motions conditioned not to intersect. This is starkly different from the subcritical ($T<T_c(q)$) behaviour. At $T_c(q)$, previous results (Bricmont--Lebowitz '87, Messager--Miracle-Sole--Ruiz--Shlosman '91) were limited to the construction and properties of the surface tension for large enough $q$. In a companion work, arXiv:2502.04129, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-disorder Dobrushin conditions. That work also develops a ``renewal picture'' \`a la Ornstein-Zernike for a suitable percolation model, which plays a central part in our study of the Potts interfaces. The latter is the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and is related to the Potts model via a chain of couplings going through the six-vertex model. In the current work, we extend the analysis to a pair of interacting order-disorder interfaces forming the separation between the two ordered phases, and couple them to a pair of well-behaved random walks conditioned not to intersect. The construction of the coupling is based on rigorously deriving entropic repulsion between the two interfaces. We also prove convergence of interfaces in the FK-percolation model at $p_c(q)$ when $q>4$.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Dober, Alexander Glazman, S\'ebastien Ott

item.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2606.02786v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper is concerned with $\alpha$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $\alpha$-stable SDE.
item.dc:creator: Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

item.title: Swapping and Switching for Markov Processes: Symmetrisation and Fast-Exchange Limits
item.description: arXiv:2607.14266v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In parallel tempering, exchanging the positions of the replicas (swapping) and exchanging the assignment of dynamics to the replicas (switching) are often used interchangeably. We study the two descriptions as stochastic processes, for Markov species (the dynamics that are exchanged) and bounded measurable exchange rates. To guarantee the Markovianity of each process under the exchanges, switching records both the positions and the label that tracks which species each replica carries; swapping records only the positions. Driving both with one exchange clock places them on a common probability space and lets us write swapping as switching with the label forgotten. This relation holds pathwise at every time and, once decomposed over the label, yields an exact identity between their transition kernels. This characterisation lets us relate, in a precise way, where the two processes agree and where they differ. We describe mainly the relation between their decay rates at finite exchange rate, and between their distributions and observables at finite and infinite exchange rate. The relation between the Markovianity of the two is particularly interesting. At finite rate, switching needs the label to be Markov, while swapping is Markov on its own. In the infinite-rate limit this reverses: swapping becomes non-tight, while switching becomes Markov on the physical coordinates alone. We illustrate all these relations on a solvable benchmark of two Brownian motions with drift under a constant exchange rate. The rich behaviour already visible in this simple case, and developed throughout the paper, suggests that the swapping mechanism is of interest in its own right, beyond the balance conditions needed in parallel tempering.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Juli\'an D\'iaz-P\'erez, Roberto Mulet

item.title: Repeated differentiation of deterministic polynomials with asymptotically radial root distributions
item.description: arXiv:2607.16954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent works of Galligo, Najnudel, and Vu (2025) and Najnudel and Vu (2026) study repeated differentiation for polynomials of the form $P(z)=p(z^m)$, where $p$ is a deterministic polynomial of degree $n$ with real, non-negative roots, in the regime where $m$ and $n$ are large. If $m\gg \log(n)$ and the root distribution of $P$ converges to a compactly supported, radial probability measure $\mu_0$, these works show that for $0\le t<1$, the root distribution of the $\lfloor nmt\rfloor$-th derivative of $P$ converges to a compactly supported probability measure $\mu_t$ given by an explicit formula for its radial quantile function. We give a substantially simplified proof of this result and also extend the result from repeated differentiation to repeated applications of the differential operator $z^a(d/dz)^b$. Our proof is based on new, sharp estimates on the roots of polynomial with real, non-negative roots in terms of the coefficients of the polynomial. We also compute the limiting root distribution in the case when $m$ is fixed and $n$ tends to infinity. Then letting $m$ tend to infinity we obtain the same limit as before. Along the way, we prove a generalization of the free multiplicative law of large numbers that is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Brian C. Hall, Daniel Perales

item.title: A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes: Well-Posedness, Positivity and Malliavin Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2607.23548v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the stochastic differential equation \[ dX_t=a\bigl(b(t)-X_t\bigr)\,dt+\bigl(\sigma_0+\sigma_1\sqrt{\phi_\eps(X_t)}\bigr)\,dZ_t^{(q,H)}, \qquad X_0=x_0, \] where $Z^{(q,H)}$ is a Hermite process of order $q\geq1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, $b$ is a periodic target, $\sigma_0>0$, and $\phi_\eps$ is a smooth positive function equal to $x+\eps$ on $[0,\infty)$. The equation is understood pathwise, in the sense of Young. We prove that it has a unique solution. We give lower bounds on the probability that the solution stays positive on $[0,T]$, for every $\sigma_1\geq0$: after a Lamperti-type change of variables, which makes the noise additive, a last-passage argument shows that the probability of reaching $0$ before $T$ is at most of order $\exp(-c\,\Lambda(m_0)^{2/q}/T^{2H/q})$, where $m_0$ is the smaller of the initial level and the minimum of the target and $\Lambda$ is the natural scale of the diffusion coefficient. For $q\le2$ and $\sigma_1=0$ we show that the solution reaches negative values with positive probability, so that no almost-sure positivity holds in that case. Finally, the solution at each time belongs to $\D^{1,\infty}$, with an explicit representation of its Malliavin derivative, and its law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. The proofs of these two results are self-contained and rely on the additive form of the equation. Numerical experiments based on a wavelet-type simulation of Hermite processes illustrate the results.
item.dc:creator: Atef Lechiheb

item.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.21805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of R\"ockner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $\Phi_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $\gamma_t = \int_0^t \Phi_r \Phi_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $\Phi_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $\Phi$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}\Phi$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same H\"older triangle of moment exponents.
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Mirafzali, Frank Proske, Razvan Marinescu

item.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequalities via Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.24687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Isoperimetric inequalities on the Boolean hypercube play a fundamental role in the analysis of Boolean functions. These inequalities have been established primarily for the uniform measure and for biased product measures, often through Fourier-analytic or inductive arguments. We develop a curvature-based semigroup framework to establish isoperimetric inequalities for measures with weakly dependent coordinates. In particular, we show that a Dobrushin-type condition, together with marginal boundedness of the distribution, implies the local Bobkov inequality, Talagrand's $L^1$--$L^2$ and variance--surface-area inequalities, the Kahn--Kalai--Linial inequality, and the Eldan--Gross inequality. Our results apply to zero-field Ising models with interaction matrix $J$ throughout the Dobrushin uniqueness regime $\|J\|_1<1$. The framework builds on discrete Bakry--\'Emery theory and gradient estimates and can also be extended to measures on Hamming slices or hypergrids.
item.dc:creator: Zejia Chen, Zongchen Chen, Xinyuan Zhang

item.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of Speed Monotonicity for the Biased Random Walk on a Galton-Watson Tree Beyond the Known Range
item.description: arXiv:2609.29894v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The speed $v(\lambda)$ of the $\lambda$-biased random walk on a supercritical Galton--Watson tree without leaves is conjectured to be nonincreasing on $[0,m)$, where $m$ is the mean offspring. For non-constant offspring, monotonicity is known only for small bias: $\lambda\le 1/1160$, $\lambda\le 1/2$, and, when every vertex has at least $m_1\ge 2$ children, $\lambda\le m_1/(1+\sqrt{1-1/m_1})$. For offspring uniform on $\{2,3\}$ ($m=2.5$) the last bound is $2/(1+\sqrt{1/2})\approx1.1716$. We prove, with computer assistance, that $v$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1.755]$ for this law. The proof has three parts. A\"id\'ekon's speed formula gives $v=(R-\lambda)/(R+\lambda)$ for an explicit functional $R$, so $v$ decreases exactly when $R/\lambda$ does; we compare $R/\lambda$ at two biases directly, which avoids differentiating the conductance. A pathwise Lipschitz bound on the conductance in $\lambda$ turns that comparison into an inequality between expectations of explicit functions. A monotone sandwich of discretised laws gives two-sided bounds on the conductance law, and each $\lambda$-cell is checked in exact rational arithmetic over bounded floating-point error, with five cells re-checked in interval arithmetic; all reduction lemmas and an exact-integer certificate across $[1.17,1.755]$ are also formally verified in Lean 4. The method stops where the crude Lipschitz bound becomes too weak; sharper control of the derivative of the conductance is what the full range needs. Code and certificates are public.
item.dc:creator: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

item.title: A zero-one law for swap-invariant events in uniform spanning forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.00938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every event invariant under swaps has probability zero or one for either the free or the wired spanning forest on any connected, locally finite, infinite network. Applications include the constancy of the number of components and of the total number of excessive ends. For the free forest, these results resolve longstanding questions of Benjamini, Lyons, Peres, and Schramm [Ann. Probab. (2001), Question 15.7] on constancy of the component count and of Lyons, Morris, and Schramm [Electron. J. Probab. (2008), Question 7.7] on the zero-one law for one-endedness. In the latter case, we obtain the stronger conclusion that the total number of excessive ends is deterministic.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Li, Yao Yu

item.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.06480v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Z_N$ be the partition function of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta>1$. Replica theory (Kondor near the critical temperature, Parisi and Rizzo at all temperatures) predicts that the probability that $N^{-1}\log Z_N$ exceeds its typical value by $\delta$ decays like $\exp(-Na\delta^{6/5})$ with an explicit $a$; Aronow and Lopatto recently proved bounds of this order. The exponent is the Legendre transform of the Parisi problem constrained to carry an atom $\theta$ at zero. We show that the constrained minimum exceeds the equilibrium free energy by $c_\beta\theta^5(1+o(1))$, where $c_\beta=\frac{9}{640}\beta^3\rho_\beta(0)^{-3}$ and $\rho_\beta(0)>0$ is the density at zero of the Parisi measure. With the fractional-moment formula this gives the exponent $\frac56(6c_\beta)^{-1/5}\delta^{6/5}(1+o(1))$ as $N\to\infty$ and then $\delta\to0$. The constrained minimizer has a marginal first positive contact, to leading order at $3\theta/(2\rho_\beta(0))$ with an atom $\theta/2$. This plateau calculus applies to every mixture with $\xi'''(0)=0$ whose Parisi measure accumulates at zero; a small field $h$ opens a gap of order $|h|^{2/3}$, and an atom of the Parisi measure at zero, present in every pure $p$-spin model with $p\ge3$, makes the rate leave zero linearly. Near criticality the constant tends to Kondor's value $9/5120$ and the marginal regime ends at a de Almeida-Thouless threshold. For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every $\beta>1$, a finite-step curvature inequality from an unrefereed preprint shows that every constrained minimizer either has an interval of positive contacts, all marginal, or has exactly two atoms, and that the marginal regime ends at a unique de Almeida-Thouless threshold $\theta_c(\beta)$. The laws at every $\beta>1$ use that the Parisi measure accumulates at zero, a theorem of Lopatto also proved in earlier work of the author.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.15950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $\tau\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-2 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $\tau\ge0$, including the deterministic case $\tau=0$. At each fixed $\tau>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/\tau}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $\tau\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.
item.dc:creator: Junho Lee, Promit Ghosal

item.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
item.description: arXiv:2610.19233v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $\nu>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+\nu+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.
item.dc:creator: Steven P. Clark

item.title: Infinite-variation L\'evy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
item.description: arXiv:2610.20916v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every real L\'evy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a L\'evy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Gonz\'alez C\'azares, David Kramer-Bang, Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c

item.title: Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections
item.description: arXiv:2610.33199v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and R\'enyi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. Although the limiting distribution was studied in earlier works, we give a simple and self-contained proof that relates it to the cutoff phenomenon for an absorbing Markov chain. We also provide an alternative expression for the cutoff window in terms of the Lambert $W$ function.
item.dc:creator: Maria Eliza Castro, Rodrigo Marinho

item.title: Extending the V-sequence reduction to arbitrary independent distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A decision maker observes independent random variables sequentially and must stop at an overall maximum, with ties counted as wins. In this short note, we extend the $V$-sequence reduction of Allaart and Islas (2016) to arbitrary independent distributions, including atoms, which were not covered by the original reduction. We spread atoms over ordered intervals without increasing the optimal win probability, then apply the continuous reduction. The resulting comparison uses a common threshold and a common splitting probability at that threshold. It also recovers the sharp universal lower bound previously established by Hill and Kennedy (1992).
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e A. Islas

item.title: The second reconstruction transition for random graphs from 2-neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2611.07890v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, with high probability, the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ is reconstructible up to isomorphism from the multiset of its rooted induced 2-neighborhoods whenever $p\geq n^{-3/4}(\log n)^3$. Together with the non-reconstructibility result of Johnston, Kronenberg, Roberts and Scott, our result locates the second reconstruction transition at the scale $p=n^{-3/4}$ up to polylogarithmic factors, resolving a question they posed. Our proof relies on a global rigidity argument exploiting 5-cycle constraints.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Chen

item.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08208v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.
item.dc:creator: Tim Johnston

item.title: Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.13809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unproved before. Our approach (called the SLE arc test) is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyan Xie

item.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2112.14662v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $\rho(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarn\'ik-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Sodin

item.title: Testing the number of common factors by bootstrapped sample covariance matrix in high-dimensional factor models and errata
item.description: arXiv:2202.06188v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the impact of bootstrap procedure on the eigenvalue distributions of the sample covariance matrix under a high-dimensional factor structure. We provide asymptotic distributions for the top eigenvalues of bootstrapped sample covariance matrix under mild conditions. After bootstrap, the spiked eigenvalues which are driven by common factors will converge weakly to Gaussian limits after proper scaling and centralization. However, the largest non-spiked eigenvalue is mainly determined by the order statistics of the bootstrap resampling weights, and follows extreme value distribution. Based on the disparate behavior of the spiked and non-spiked eigenvalues, we propose innovative methods to test the number of common factors. Indicated by extensive numerical and empirical studies, the proposed methods perform reliably and convincingly under the existence of both weak factors and cross-sectionally correlated errors. Our technical details contribute to random matrix theory on spiked covariance model with convexly decaying density and unbounded support, or with general elliptical distributions.
item.dc:creator: Long Yu, Peng Zhao, Wang Zhou

item.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2305.13037v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Ferrari, Stefano Olla

item.title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fourth-order SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
item.description: arXiv:2501.18240v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the strong numerical approximation for a fourth-order stochastic nonlinear SPDE driven by space-time white noise on {{$d=1,2,3$}}-dimensional torus. We consider its full discretisation with a spectral Galerkin scheme in space and Euler scheme in time. We show the convergence with almost spatial rate $2-\frac{d}{2}$ and $\frac{6-d}{4} \wedge 1$-temporal rate obtained mainly via \it{Stochastic Sewing} technique.
item.dc:creator: Dirk Bl\"omker, Chengcheng Ling, Johannes Rimmele

item.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2502.20871v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Averboukh, Ekaterina Kolpakova

item.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
item.description: arXiv:2603.10655v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well-documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here we analyze intermittent L\'evy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the L\'evy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ($\mu = 2$) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area $\Delta$ in a domain of volume $n$, the optimal expected detection time scales as $n/\Delta$, and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other L\'evy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Stromieri, Emanuele Natale, Amos Korman

item.title: Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature and Edge-Connectivity of Hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.06029v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a local geometric criterion ensuring that the edge-connectivity of a hypergraph equals its minimum incidence degree: every locally finite connected simple $r$-uniform linear hypergraph with $r\ge3$ and nonnegative Lin--Lu--Yau curvature has this property. Among the various extensions of Ollivier--Ricci curvature to hypergraphs, we work with the equal-edges random walk on hypergraphs \cite{CoupetteEtAl2023}. Moreover, we show that both uniformity and linearity are essential: if either assumption is removed, there exist positively curved hypergraphs for which the gap between minimum incidence degree and edge-connectivity is arbitrarily large. For adjacent vertices in any locally finite simple hypergraph, the Ollivier--Ricci idleness function is concave and piecewise affine with at most three affine pieces, and is affine on $[1/2,1]$. In particular, $\kappa_{\LLY}=2\kappa_{1/2}$, which we use to verify positive curvature in the two families of examples.
item.dc:creator: Qing Xia

item.title: Squarefree polynomials with missing digits
item.description: arXiv:2608.17892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an asymptotic formula for squarefree polynomials over a finite field whose coefficients are in $\{0,1\}$. This resolves a function-field analogue of a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Mauduit and S\'ark\"ozy. More generally, we estimate the probability of a polynomial $\sum \varepsilon_it^i$ being squarefree, where $\varepsilon_i$ are random variables sampled according to measures on $\mathbb{F}_q$.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Bazlov

item.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
item.description: arXiv:2609.18269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.
item.dc:creator: Alex Prygarin, Claudelle Capasia Madjuogang Sandeu, Karam Shekh Yusuf

item.title: Quenched Growth of Normal Matrices and Harmonic Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.03912v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The eigenvalues of a large normal random matrix form a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. At fixed weight, the spectral droplet grows with the matrix rank, and its semiclassical density increment is harmonic measure. We freeze an $N$-eigenvalue configuration and sample $M$ further eigenvalues using the projection onto polynomials of degree less than $N+M$ that vanish at the frozen points. Their conditional law is an exact polynomial ensemble in the potential of the frozen charges. For a regular analytic droplet, we prove that the spatial distribution of the new eigenvalues converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary when $M/\log N\to\infty$ and $M/N\to0$. This convergence holds conditionally on the frozen spectrum, outside a set of frozen configurations whose probability tends to zero. The equilibrium process formed from orthogonal polynomials of degrees $N,\ldots,N+M-1$ has the same limit. An exact finite-rank identity relates polynomial moments of the conditional mean to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum, with a remainder from polynomial modes of degree $N+M$ and above.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Alekseev

item.title: Learning controls in mean field games: the fictitious play and related gradient descent
item.description: arXiv:2610.06292v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate two learning procedures and their relationship to the formation of equilibrium in potential mean field games (MFGs). The first one is a version of the fictitious play in which players observe directly the actions (controls) of other players and learn the distribution of the MFG through an update rules on controls. This leads to a new iterative procedure which converges for a wide class of potential MFGs of controls, even in the presence of common noise. On the other hand we also consider the learning procedure of a principal agent trying to solve a mean field control problem with only local gradient information. We prove that under very general assumption, the gradient descent of such agent converges to a solution of the associated potential MFG.
item.dc:creator: Charles Meynard (LJAD)

item.title: A perturbation theory for Feynman-Kac models and their particle interpretations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a perturbation analysis of Feynman--Kac models, describing how local errors introduced at each step of the Feynman--Kac recursion propagate over time. Under general conditions on the potential functions and the Markov transitions, which are shown to hold for a large class of state-space models, we prove that the global error for any time horizon $T\geq 1$ is bounded by $C\,\Delta_T\log(1+\Delta_T^{-1})$, where $\Delta_T$ is the largest local error; this bound holds both for the prediction and the updated models. These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Del Moral, Mathieu Gerber

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: similar circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Roshka

item.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and proofs of this have recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever all $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. Consequently, for the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$, the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$. These results rest on the annulus crossing bound of Ding, Huang and Yang, used on one finite annulus where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation, and on a sign-cluster argument with Ginibre's inequality for anisotropic planar energies. Explicit constants of another isotropic proof give decay for $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. For $n\ge4$ and $|J^i-1|\le\delta$ with $\delta$ small, at $\beta\le(1-\varepsilon)|\log\delta|/(2\pi)$ spin one-point functions decay exponentially away from the boundary under every boundary condition, and two-point functions decay, both on the scale $e^{\pi\beta+O(\sqrt{\beta\log\beta})}$. This is the $O(4)$ threshold: for $n=4$ it matches the renormalization-group crossover to leading order; for $n\ge5$ it lies below the prediction. This part is conditional on estimates of a recent manuscript on the $O(4)$ model, which the proof transfers to anisotropic couplings at one scale; only odd observables transfer.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.09753v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
item.dc:creator: William Verreault, Max Wenqiang Xu
